title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U = U_{0,3} = P^1_C minus {0,1,infinity}. Pi_{0,3} = pi_1(U) is free on two generators, with loops l_0, l_1, l_infinity satisfying l_0 l_1 l_infinity = 1. T_{0,3} (order 12, about S_3 x Z/2) is the group of holomorphic and antiholomorphic automorphisms of U. Gamma_{0,3} is the extension 1 -> Pi_{0,3} -> Gamma_{0,3} -> T_{0,3} -> 1, i.e. the group of all lifts of these automorphisms to the universal cover (the upper half plane). Concretely Gamma_{0,3} is PGL(2,Z), the extended (2,3,infinity) triangle group, with Pi_{0,3} = the image of Gamma(2) in PSL(2,Z).

On the previous page Grothendieck lifted each torsion element of T_{0,3} to a torsion element of Gamma_{0,3}: sigma_i, tau, tau'_i, and an order-3 element rho over rho-dot. That page also recalls the 'general theory': Pi-conjugacy classes of torsion lifts of an element correspond to connected components of its fixed-point set in U.

On this page:
(1) Other lifts of rho-dot. He writes (23): rho_i = tau_i rho tau_i^{-1}, with rho_0 = l_inf^{-1} rho = rho l_1^{-1}, rho_1 = l_0^{-1} rho = rho l_inf^{-1}, rho_inf = l_1^{-1} rho = rho l_0^{-1}. These encode that conjugation by rho permutes the loops cyclically: l_0 -> l_1 -> l_inf -> l_0. The margin relations rho rho_0 rho^{-1} = rho_1 (and its cyclic shifts) follow, and rho rho_0 rho^{-1} = l_inf rho_0 l_inf^{-1}. So the three rho_i are Pi-conjugate to each other. They are not Pi-conjugate to rho, because rho-dot has two fixed points in U, -j and -jbar, giving two classes of lifts; conjugating by an antiholomorphic tau_i swaps them.
(2) Formula (24). The centralisers in Pi_{0,3} of all the chosen torsion lifts (sigma_i, rho, tau_i, tau'_i) are trivial. Justification: the relevant fixed-point components are simply connected. For holomorphic elements they are isolated points; for antiholomorphic involutions they are real intervals of P^1(R) minus {0,1,infinity}. The centraliser is pi_1 of the fixed component.
(3) Finite subgroups. The points of U with nontrivial stabiliser in T_{0,3} form two orbits:
- {2, -1, 1/2}, with stabiliser of order 4. For the point 2 this is D_2 = Z/2 x Z/2, generated by sigma_0-dot (z -> z/(z-1)) and tau_0-dot (complex conjugation).
- {-jbar, -j}, i.e. e^{+-i pi/3}, with stabiliser of order 6, namely S'_3 = D_3.
Both subgroups were already lifted into Gamma_{0,3} as finite subgroups. The general theory then says that Pi-conjugacy classes of liftings of a finite subgroup H correspond to fixed points of H in U. For D_2^{(0)} there is one class (the point 2); for D_3 there are two (-jbar and -j), and the second class is obtained by conjugating by any tau_i.

Purpose. This is part of an explicit, combinatorial presentation of Gamma_{0,3} and its torsion. The next page uses it to identify Gamma_{0,3} with the unoriented triangulated cartographic group and with SL(2,Z)/PGL(2,Z), presumably as the base case for the 'équation des lacets' and the Teichmüller tower in genus 0.
errors: No mathematical error found. The identities rho_0 = l_inf^{-1} rho = rho l_1^{-1} etc. and the margin conjugation relations are mutually consistent (they encode rho l_0 rho^{-1} = l_1, rho l_1 rho^{-1} = l_inf, rho l_inf rho^{-1} = l_0).
Minor imprecision: the phrase 'Pi-conjugués entre eux' is justified by the margin relations only after noting that rho rho_0 rho^{-1} = l_inf rho_0 l_inf^{-1}. Grothendieck leaves this step implicit.

ideas.what: Pi-conjugacy classes of torsion lifts of an element g of a finite group acting on a K(pi,1) correspond to connected components of the fixed locus of g; the centraliser in Pi of a lift is pi_1 of the corresponding component.
ideas.modern_name: Topological/real analogue of the section conjecture (sections over finite subgroups vs fixed points; cf. real section conjecture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical orbifold/equivariant topology; in the anabelian setting Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings; real section conjecture studied by Mochizuki, Pál, Wickelgren, Stix
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) and La Longue Marche (1981), discussion of torsion in Teichmüller groups (exact location unsure)

ideas.what: Explicit alternate lifts rho_i = tau_i rho tau_i^{-1} of the order-3 element, with the cyclic action of rho on the loops l_0, l_1, l_inf.
ideas.modern_name: Torsion classes in PGL(2,Z) / extended (2,3,infinity) triangle group

ideas.what: Stabilisers of the special points of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} under S_3 x complex conjugation: D_2 at {2,-1,1/2} and D_3 at {-j,-jbar}, together with lifting of these finite subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Elliptic points / maximal finite subgroups of PGL(2,Z)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine bookkeeping page: it lists torsion lifts and finite subgroups of the extended genus-0 Teichmüller group (essentially PGL(2,Z)) using the known fixed-point correspondence. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Top line: the three bracketed expressions are written above and refer to rho_0, rho_1, rho_inf respectively (rho_0 = l_inf^{-1} rho = rho l_1^{-1}, etc.). The last one reads l_1^{-1} rho = rho l_0^{-1}.
Formula (23) on the image is followed by 'deux à deux distincts' (a hand-reading).
'les formules cristallisées' is doubtful; likely 'les formules résultant de la théorie générale' or similar.
'Pour le pt 2 (supposé à 0)' plausibly reads 'Pour le pt 2 (associé à 0)'.
'D_2 ≃ Z/2Z × Z/2Z' is consistent with the image; the generators are written sigma_0-dot, tau_0-dot (or sigma_0, tau'_0).
'ce qui avait donné -jbar' is uncertain; it likely says the chosen lift corresponds to one of the two points.
